question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` accept scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, now that the official Chrome extension also has a dedicated `/browser/extension` relay path?
rationale: This changes a Gateway browser-origin authorization boundary and could trust all Chrome extension origins for Control UI/WebChat connections, while current docs intentionally describe full-origin allowlisting plus the global `*` as the only wildcard policy.

options.title: Keep Control UI full-origin only
options.body: Use the dedicated Chrome extension relay for the official extension and require a clearer generic-extension need before adding scheme wildcards to Control UI origins.

options.title: Approve a constrained extension wildcard
options.body: Allow only a tightly scoped `chrome-extension://*` grammar with explicit positive and negative Gateway tests and docs.

options.title: Fold into broader origin patterns
options.body: Wait for the loopback `allowedOriginPatterns` design and decide whether extension schemes belong in that same contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Keep Control UI full-origin only
recommendation.body: Use the dedicated Chrome extension relay for the official extension and require a clearer generic-extension need before adding scheme wildcards to Control UI origins.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the strongest recent and historical signals for both the Gateway origin boundary and the dedicated Chrome extension relay path.
